paragraphs.text: This he did, that he might the better insure the promise made to himself; and avert, if possible, the judgments threatened against the people by Huldah the prophetess.
paragraphs.anchor: And the king sent.

paragraphs.text: And the king went up … and all the men of Judah.] Solemnly to renew their covenant with God; a course ever found to be of singular avail in case of any common calamity felt or feared.
See 2Ki 11:14.
paragraphs.anchor: And the king stood by a pillar.

paragraphs.text: To be in communion with him, and in conformity unto him. This is elsewhere called walking with God, and walking before God.
paragraphs.anchor: To walk after the Lord.

paragraphs.text: They pretended and professed so to do; but the most of them dissembled and dealt deceitfully, not turning to God with their whole hearts, as good Jeremiah complaineth, {Jer 3:1-25} and therefore calleth upon them {Jer 4:3; Jer 4:14} to "break up their fallow ground, to circumcise themselves unto the Lord, and to wash their hearts from wickedness, that they might be saved."
paragraphs.anchor: And all the people stood to the covenant.

paragraphs.text: Ithamar’s race.
paragraphs.anchor: And the priests of the second order.

paragraphs.text: Called also Bethaven, because there had stood one of Jeroboam’s golden calves: hither therefore this good king sent the ashes of those burnt idols and their trinkets to disgrace it, and that such wicked dust might not remain in Judah, that holy land, saith Cajetan.
paragraphs.anchor: And carried the ashes of them unto Bethel.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Chemarims, Baal’s chimney-chaplains, {see Zep 1:14, with the note there} black sooty fellows, like those greasy mass priests, or abbey lubbers, amongst the Papists.
paragraphs.anchor: And he put down the idolatrous priests.

paragraphs.text: Or, Influences: a radice Nazal fluxit.
paragraphs.anchor: And to the planets.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 21:7.
paragraphs.anchor: And he brought out the grove.

paragraphs.text: The vulgar sort, the rascality, who are usually most irrational, and so most idolatrous. "Thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief," said Aaron of those that said unto him, "Make us gods," &c. {Exo 32:22-23}
paragraphs.anchor: Upon the graves of the children of the people.

paragraphs.text: Abominable brothel houses.
paragraphs.anchor: The houses of the sodomites.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Houses, aedicula, sacella textilia, as Act 19:24. There were at Ephesus that made templa portabilia, small portable temples, resembling that greater temple.
paragraphs.anchor: Where the women wove hangings.

paragraphs.text: Where, in imitation of the heathens, they had set their tutelar and guardian gods, and had their fans profana.
paragraphs.anchor: The high places of the gates.

paragraphs.text: A great man, but none of the best. He had a good name; but Josiah might have said to him, as Alexander did to a soldier of his own name, but a coward, Either change thy name, or put on more courage; so, more piety.
paragraphs.anchor: Of Joshua the governor of the city.

paragraphs.text: Care was taken for their maintenance: (1.) As Levites; (2.) As penitents; though, for service at the altar, they were laid aside. Penitency and punishment are words of one derivation, and are near of kin.
paragraphs.anchor: But they did eat of the unleavened bread.

paragraphs.text: A pleasant valley near to Jerusalem, but, for the abominable abuse of it, taken afterwards for hell, {Isa 30:33 Mat 5:22} a place of torments, without end, and past imagination.
paragraphs.anchor: And he defiled Tophet.

paragraphs.text: Not statues of horses and chariots dedicated to the sun, as some interpret it; sed equos veros et vivos, living and light horses dedicated to the sun, after the Persian mode, ωσπερ το ταχιστον τω ταχοτατω θεω, as the swiftest creature to the swiftest god. {a} These Josiah caused to be killed. Macrobius telleth us that the Syrians called God Adad (Achad, he should have said); that is, One, quia unus est sol - sic dictus quasi Solus - aeque ac Deus in mundo: because, as there is but one sun in the world, so but one God. But how many gods they worshipped, see learned Mr Selden, De diis Syris.
paragraphs.anchor: And he took away the horses.

paragraphs.text: Qui fuit imberbis, qualis est sol, saith Villapandus; {b} a beardless officer for a beardless god. The Persians called the sun Mithras and Apollo. This Nathanmelech, though a courtier, thought it an honour to be groom of the sun’s stable.
paragraphs.anchor: Nathanmelech the chamberlain.

paragraphs.text: Chrysostom saith that Peter, for his zeal, was like a man made all of fire walking among stubble. Josiah was surely so. Angelomus saith, that herein he represented Christ, who, by the fire of the last day, shall destroy all impiety, and not suffer any defiled one to enter into his kingdom.
paragraphs.anchor: And burnt the chariots of the sun with fire.

paragraphs.text: {a} Pausan. Herodot. Xenoph.
{b} Lib iii. cap. 32, in Ezech., cap. 40, p. 221.
See Jer 19:13 Zep 1:5. Ahaz was ειδωλομανης.
paragraphs.anchor: And the altars that were on the top.

paragraphs.text: These, after his repentance, he cast out of the city, {2Ch 33:15} but not so thoroughly abolished; hence they became snares to his successors.
paragraphs.anchor: And the altars which Manasseh had made.

paragraphs.text: Or, Ran from thence; quam citissime potuit discedens illinc, {a} he got out of those loathsome places as soon as he could.
paragraphs.anchor: And brake them down from thence.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The town ditch.
paragraphs.anchor: Into the brook Kidron

paragraphs.text: {a} Vatab.

There they had boldly set up their abominable idols in mount Olivet, even in the sight of the Lord; so that he never looked out of the sanctuary but he saw that vile hill, which, therefore, he here calleth not Har Hammisha, {a} the mount of annointing, but Har Hammaschith, {b} the mount of corruption. Est tacita paranomasia; item allusio, item detorsio.
paragraphs.anchor: And the high places that were before Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: So called, because the people had there corrupted themselves, as Deu 32:5; and yet afterwards it became our Saviour’s oratory, or usual place of prayer, This showeth, that places which have been abused to idolatry, may yet afterwards be used for God’s service. As for that which we read, Deu 12:2-3, "Ye shall utterly destroy all the places," &c., divines answer, that that was a temporary ordinance, and a part of Moses’s polity, now abrogated.
paragraphs.anchor: Of the mount of corruption.

paragraphs.text: But, after his repentance, had demolished, likely; though, by the idolatrous princes that came after him, they were rebuilded, and called still by his name.
paragraphs.anchor: Which Solomon had builded.

paragraphs.text: {a} Of Mashach.
{b} Of Shacah.

He made no spare of any of those idols and monuments of idolatry, though there wanted not some about him, doubtless, that could have wished it otherwise, and moved him to spare those goodly horses and chariots of the sun, &c. But he was resolved to make a hand with them all. We may give peace to buy truth, but we may not give truth to buy peace.
paragraphs.anchor: And he brake in pieces the images.

paragraphs.text: It is probable that the king of Babylon, when he sent home Manasseh, gave him also dominion of the greatest part of the country of Samaria, indenting with him to defend the same against the Egyptian. Howsoever, good Josiah faileth not to root out idolatry in all those parts also, {2Ki 23:19} it being an abandoned country, which, in a manner, had no lord at all.
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the altar that was at Bethel.

paragraphs.text: That had been foreseen and foretold three hundred years at least before. {1Ki 13:2} Intervention ofttimes breaks no square in the divine decrees. Our blind eyes see nothing but that which toucheth their lids: the quick sight of God’s prescience sees that as present which is a world afar off.
paragraphs.anchor: He sent and took the bones.

paragraphs.text: This was not the name Jehovah, or the sign of the cross, as some have doted; but either some pillar, orelse gravestone, with a superscription showing who lay there buried: such as was that on Scaliger’s tomb, Scaligeri quod reliquum est, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: What title is that that I see?

paragraphs.text: Historiae fidae monitrices: monumenta quasi mentem monentia. But the greatest wonder is, saith one, that these Bethelites, so well knowing what they here do relate to Josiah, were not moved to relinquish their idolatrous worship. But most probably they believed not till they saw it fulfilled.
paragraphs.anchor: And the men of the citytold him.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 23:15.
paragraphs.anchor: And did to them according.

paragraphs.text: And burnt men’s bones.] Hence Papists would prove the lawfulness of unburying dead heretics, as they call us, and burning their bones; as they dealt here by Grosthead, bishop of Lincoln, Paulus Phagius, Bucer’s wife, &c. But Josiah’s act is justified by the prophecy, whereby he was appointed so to do; and the Lord would have it so done, to show the abomination wherein he had idolaters, and for a demonstration of their damnation in hell.

2Ch 35:1. If the passover had been neglected, the law, the sacrifices had been in vain. No true Israelite might want whether this monument of their deliverance past, or this type of the Messiah to come. Rather than fail, Josiah’s bounty shall supply to Judah lambs for their paschal devotion. No alms is so acceptable as that whereby the soul is furthered. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Keep the passover.

paragraphs.text: {a} Dr Hall.

viz., For concourse of people, and solemnity of the service. Tremellius rendereth it thus: Although there was not holden such a passover as this, viz., with such preparation, devotion, and reformation of religion; yet, {2Ki 23:26} "God turned not away from his wrath," &c., as being implacably bent and unchangeably resolved upon their utter ruin.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely there was not holden such a passover

paragraphs.text: viz., Of his reign, but in the twenty-sixth of his age.
paragraphs.anchor: But in the eighteenth year

paragraphs.text: q.d., Josiah did all that might be done to prevent that utter devastation of his country foretold by the prophets; but the decree was even "ready to bring forth," and there was no reversing or impeding it. {Zep 2:2} See 2Ki 21:10-15.
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the workers with familiar spirits

paragraphs.text: Heb., Teraphim; these were properly their household gods, saith Vatablus.
paragraphs.anchor: And the images.

paragraphs.text: Here he narrowly spied out everything that was amiss, to reform it, as being his own proper dominion, and his chief charge. Latini videndum dicunt,
paragraphs.anchor: That were spied in the land of Judah and Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: “ Aedibus in propriis quae recta aut prava gerantur. ”
He was a matchless man, a peerless prince, the world’s paragon,
paragraphs.anchor: And like unto him was there no king, &c.

paragraphs.text: “ Hic regum decus et iuvenum flos, spesque bonorum.
Deliciae saecli et gloria gentis erat. ”
As Cardan singeth of our Edward VI, a second Josiah, as all good men acknowledged. See 2Ki 18:5.
And with all his might.] Heb., With his utmost vehemency, strength, and diligence; he did all that he could do.
See on 2Ki 23:22.
paragraphs.anchor: Notwithstanding the Lord, &c.

paragraphs.text: His sin was pardoned upon his repentance, but his reproach was not altogether wiped away, as Pro 6:33. The stain of it was like iron mould, which nothing can fetch out. His posterity also, yea, and the generality of the people, persisting in Manasseh’s sins, were justly punishable for the same. The Corinthians were accessory to the sin of the incestuous person, because they bewailed it not; {1Co 5:2} and shall not we of this age smart for those bloody Marian days, if we lament not, and so disclaim them?
paragraphs.anchor: Because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal.

paragraphs.text: Who was now grown worse than Israel, {Jer 3:11} and was therefore worse, because she should have been better warned by the others’ harms.
paragraphs.anchor: I will remove Judah also out of my sight.

paragraphs.text: See 1Ki 15:23.
paragraphs.anchor: Now the rest of the acts, &c.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Claudus Pharaoh, the club-foot, so called for distinction. Tamerlane was likewise lame of one foot.
paragraphs.anchor: In his days Pharaohnechoh

paragraphs.text: Nabopolassar, king of Babylon, who had subdued the Assyrians, and gloried in that noble title, king of Assyria. See 2Ki 20:12.
paragraphs.anchor: Went up against the king of Assyria.

paragraphs.text: i.e., To the city Carchemish bordering thereupon.
paragraphs.anchor: To the river Euphrates

paragraphs.text: This was rashly done. The soldier’s motto is, Nec temere nec timide. Josiah fearing more to be counted timorous than temerarious, rushed upon his own death; not so much as advising with that famous prophet Jeremiah, or Zephaniah, or Urijah, the prophets then living; besides a whole college of seers. Sometimes both grace and wit are asleep in the holiest and wariest breasts. Perhaps he feared lest the Egyptian, aliud agens, should seize upon his country; or lest it lying between these two mighty monarchs, should be made the field or seat of their war, and so should be ground to powder, as grain between two millstones.
paragraphs.anchor: And king Josiah went against him.

paragraphs.text: In this respect Abulenais excuseth Josiah from all blame; but that cannot be. See 2Ch 35:22. God had a holy hand in it, howsoever, for the just punishment of that sinful nation, way being now made by the death of this good prince for God’s judgments to rush in upon them with full force.

That is, He, by his archers, gave him his deathly wound at Megiddo, forty-four miles from Jerusalem, whither he was by his servants bright, but died by the way, and was greatly lamented. {2Ch 35:24 Zec 12:11} So was that thrice noble king of Sweden slain in Germany, yet not without the victory; which made one say,
paragraphs.anchor: And he slew him.

paragraphs.text: “Upon this place the great Gustavus died,
Whilst Victory lay bleeding by his side.”

i.e., At the first encounter, as 2Ki 14:8, priusquam inter se acies concurrerent, saith Sulpitius; before the battle began. Whilst he was setting the battle in array, riding from one wing to another, and giving instructions, saith Josephus, an Egyptian archer slew him, and together with him all the felicity of that state, which was thenceforth known, as Thebes was after the death of Epaminondas, by their calamities only.
paragraphs.anchor: When he had seen him

paragraphs.text: Mortuum, i.e., Moribundum, a dying man. See on 2Ki 23:29.
paragraphs.anchor: And his servants carried him in a chariot dead.

paragraphs.text: Lest Pharaoh at his return finding no king, should seize upon the kingdom; but this greatly provoked the conqueror, to whom they should rather have sought for peace and liberty to make them a new king.
paragraphs.anchor: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz.

paragraphs.text: He was younger than his brother Jehoiakim, {2Ki 23:36} got the kingdom from him by a popular faction, likely, and it proved accordingly. Some think him to have been called Shallum at first, {Jer 22:11} and that the people changed his name Melioris ominis causa; because Shallum king of Israel had reigned but one month only ere he was slain by Menahem. {2Ki 15:13}
paragraphs.anchor: Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 19:2-9.
paragraphs.anchor: And he did evil.

paragraphs.text: He deposed him; to show that he had now the disposal of the kingdom. Or, Because he reigned, sc., without his good leave and liking.
paragraphs.anchor: That he might not reign.

paragraphs.text: That is, God shall arise: so his good father Josiah named him, but he proved a degenerate plant; his father trembled and humbled himself at the hearing of the law, but he cut in pieces the prophecy of Jeremiah, and sought for him and Baruch to the shambles; but the Lord hid them.
paragraphs.anchor: Made Eliakim.

paragraphs.text: Memoriae causa, saith one interpreter; to show his sovereignty, saith another. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And turned his name.

paragraphs.text: According to the prophecy of Jeremiah, {Jer 22:11-12} who taxeth him there for covetousneas, ambition, and other vices, hastening the consummation or consumption of all, according to the signification of his other name, Shallum.
paragraphs.anchor: And died there.

paragraphs.text: {a} Ut Iehovae victoriam acceptam se referre testaretur, &c. - Ussher.
Though he received, likely, from his subjects no less sums of curses than of coin.
paragraphs.anchor: He exacted.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 23:31.
paragraphs.anchor: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old.

paragraphs.text: To all his former evils he added this, that he slew Urijah the prophet. {Jer 26:20; Jer 26:23}
paragraphs.anchor: And he did that which was evil.
